landmarks.name: Bayterek Tower
landmarks.writeup: A symbol of Astana (Nur-Sultan), representing a mythical tree of life and a golden egg from Kazakh folklore.

wiki.extract: Baiterek is a monument and observation tower in Astana, the capital city of Kazakhstan. A tourist attraction popular with foreign visitors and Kazakhs, it is emblematic of the city, which became capital of the country in 1997. The tower is located on Nurjol Boulevard, and is considered a symbol of post-independence Kazakhstan.

landmarks.name: Charyn Canyon
landmarks.writeup: A natural canyon known for its striking rock formations, often compared to the Grand Canyon.

wiki.extract: Charyn Canyon, also known as the Sharyn Canyon is a canyon on the Charyn River in Kazakhstan. It is located about 200 km (120 mi) east of Almaty, close to the Kazakh–Chinese border. The canyon is roughly 154 km (96 mi) in length. It is part of the Charyn National Park established on 23 February 2004 and is located within the territory of the Uygur, Raiymbek, and Enbekshikazakh Districts of the Almaty Region. The canyon features many formations formed by the weathering of sedimentary rock. Though it is much smaller than the Grand Canyon, it has been described as being equally impressive.

landmarks.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this 14th-century mausoleum is an important example of Timurid architecture.

wiki.extract: The Mausoleum of Khawaja Ahmed Yasawi is a mausoleum in the city of Turkestan, in southern Kazakhstan. The structure was commissioned in 1389 by Timur, who ruled the area as part of the expansive Timurid Empire, to replace a smaller 12th-century mausoleum of the famous Turkic poet and Sufi mystic, Khoja Ahmed Yasawi (1093–1166). However, construction was halted with the death of Timur in 1405.

landmarks.name: Almaty Central Mosque
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, known for its impressive architecture and cultural significance.

wiki.extract: Almaty Central Mosque is one of the largest mosques in Almaty, and in Kazakhstan. Designed to accommodate 7,000 worshippers, it was built on the site of the old mosque that dated to 1890 and caught fire in 1987.

landmarks.name: Altai Mountains
landmarks.writeup: A mountain range offering diverse landscapes and rich biodiversity, important for both nature and cultural heritage.

wiki.extract: The Altai Mountains are a mountain range in Central Asia, where Russia, China, Mongolia, and Kazakhstan converge, and where the rivers Irtysh and Ob have their headwaters. The highest summit of the range is Belukha, whose summit reaches 4,506 m above sea level. The massif merges with the Sayan Mountains in the northeast, and gradually becomes lower in the southeast, where it merges into the high plateau of the Gobi Desert. In the southwest, it is separated from the higher Tian Shan range by the Junggar Basin. It spans from about 45° to 52° N and from about 84° to 99° E.

cultural_events.name: Nauryz
cultural_events.writeup: The traditional Persian New Year celebrated on March 21, marking the arrival of spring with festivities and rituals.

wiki.extract: Nowruz is New Year's Day on the Iranian calendars, including the currently used Solar Hijri calendar. Historically, it has been observed by Iranian peoples, but is now celebrated by many Persianate cultures worldwide. It is a festival based on the Northern Hemisphere spring equinox, and thus usually coincides with a date between 19 March and 22 March on the Gregorian calendar.

cultural_events.name: Almaty Apple Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrates the region's historical connection to the origin of the apple, featuring local produce and cultural performances.

cultural_events.name: Eurasian Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing films from Kazakhstan and neighboring countries, promoting regional cinema.

wiki.extract: Heaven – my abode is a film by Ayub Shahobiddinov. It is awarded as "the best director" film by New York Eurasian Film Festival in 2013. The film is produced by the order of the Uzbekkino National Agency in the film studio of Uzbekfilm. The film received the Grand Prix of "Golden Vine" at Kinoshock Film Festival in Russia.

food_writeup: Kazakh cuisine is rich in meat dishes, especially lamb and horse meat, often prepared as beshbarmak, a traditional dish of boiled meat served with noodles. Dairy products like kumis (fermented mare's milk) are also popular.
brief_history: Kazakhstan has a history of nomadic tribes and was part of the Silk Road. It was incorporated into the Russian Empire in the 18th century and later became a Soviet republic. It declared independence in 1991 following the dissolution of the USSR.
current_conflicts: Kazakhstan is generally stable with no active internal or external conflicts, though it faces challenges related to regional security and economic diversification.

commentary.inflation_management: The National Bank moved to inflation targeting in 2015 alongside a free float of the tenge, after years of a managed peg. Inflation was 17.2% in 2008, moderated to 5-8% in the early 2010s, then spiked to 14.6% in 2016 after the tenge's 2015 devaluation, easing to 5.3% by 2019. The 2022 shock drove it to 15.0% (14.5% in 2023), and the IMF projects 11.4% for 2025, still well above the 5% target. Dollarization and administered prices complicate transmission, and the central bank has kept policy tight to rebuild credibility.
commentary.debt_management: Public debt is low and has stayed so: 6.7% of GDP in 2006, rising only to 26.4% in 2020 on COVID and to a projected 24.6% in 2025. The sovereign wealth fund (Samruk-Kazyna/National Fund) is the real fiscal buffer, absorbing oil windfalls; the 2022 surge took GDP to $225.5bn and a projected $302.8bn by 2025. Banking-sector cleanups (notably after the 2009 BTA default) were handled off the sovereign balance sheet. Debt sustainability is comfortable; the issue is the non-oil deficit and fund drawdowns.

key_events.event: Banking crisis; BTA Bank's 2009 default was one of the largest emerging-market restructurings.
Commodity boom took GDP to $133.4bn before the crisis hit.
Oil collapse and Russian ruble crisis forced the tenge float in August 2015; inflation hit 14.6% in 2016.
Nazarbayev resigned after three decades; Tokayev succeeded him.
January unrest ('Bloody January') shook the regime; oil windfall then repaired finances.
Diversification and Middle Corridor trade pushed GDP toward a projected $302.8bn.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Kazakhstan's base case is solid: moderate debt, large buffers, and growth from oil, uranium, and transit trade, with inflation hopefully converging to target. Risks are oil-price dependence, the political transition's durability after 2022's unrest, and exposure to Russia (trade, the Caspian pipeline, secondary sanctions). If diversification and governance reforms advance, upside is real; if oil falls and buffers are drawn down, the old vulnerabilities return. Debt is not a constraint.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
